chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام saying: “No, by Allah! A knowledgeable one is never ignorant, such that he would know one thing and be ignorant of another thing.”

Then he said: “Allah is more majestic, mightier, and more generous than to obligate obedience to a servant while veiling from him the knowledge of His heaven and His earth.” Then he said: “That is not veiled from him.”

key_terms.يَفْرِضَ: to make obligatory or impose as a duty

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Imam’s comprehensive knowledge in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the one whose obedience Allah has made obligatory is not left ignorant of matters relevant to his divinely appointed role. It presents the Imam’s knowledge as part of divine wisdom, declaring that Allah would not command obedience to such a servant while concealing from him the knowledge of the heaven and the earth.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Hamza who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! A knowledgeable one<sup>asws</sup> cannot happen to be ignorant, ever, that he<sup>asws</sup> would be a knower of something and be ignorant of something’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Majestic, and more Mighty, and more Benevolent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Necessitate the obedience of a servant, and then Veil from him<sup>asws</sup> the knowledge of His<sup>azwj</sup> sky and His<sup>azwj</sup> earth’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: (Indeed) ‘Nothing is Hidden from him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu Hamzah who has that he heard abu Ja‘far (a.s.) say the following.
“No, I swear by Allah, the scholar (who possesses Divine authority) is never ignorant or knowledgeable in something and ignorant of other things.

The Imam (a.s.) then said, “Allah, the Most Holy, Most High and Most Gracious, is far exalted and above imposing the obedience of a servant (of His) on the others and then hide the knowledge of things in the heavens and on earth from him and then say, “Do not hide that from him.”
